b: ^"Wendel. The provisions are mine. The prices are the roads' fault."
^Wendel is on the Mule's step with a mug, off the clock. "Shop's shut. Ask me about lamp oil in the morning and I'll tell you it's gone up."

s0: ^"Lamp oil's up a copper. Before you ask, it's the roads."
s1: ^"Rope's cheaper than it was. Nobody's buying rope. They're buying lamp oil."
s2: ^"Somebody asked for a map of the barrows. I sell bread."

b: ^"Bess Hale. It's my name over the door, and my father's, and it's my arm doing the work. No, I'm not the Captain's. He says it first, usually."
^"Forge is banked for the night. Buy me a drink and I'll tell you what's wrong with your sword."

s0: ^"The forge is open. Bring me what you wear and I'll make it better. Bring me what you won't, and I'll make it cinders."
s1: ^"That edge has seen bone. Bone's hard on an edge. So are skeletons."
s2: ^"Father says hello. Father says it from a chair."

b: ^"Col. I drive the Greyholt cart. Drove it the long way round the barrows a whole month, a day out each way. Just so you know."

s0: ^"Barrows road's open. Half a day to Greyholt. Half a day! I'll not know what to do with the other half."
s1: ^"I went past where they stood. Nothing there now but the road, and my old wagon in the ditch. I'll have that back, thank you."

b: ^"There's fewer of them on the barrows road. I counted. Didn't stop to count properly, mind."

s0: ^"The horse still shies at the mounds. So do I. Neither of us will say so."
s1: ^"A day out of the way, both ways, for a month. Somebody ought to pay me for that day. Nobody will."
s2: ^"Saw one standing in the road at dusk last week. It saluted. I didn't."
s3: ^"That's my wagon on its side by the barrows road. They didn't hurt me. They just stood in front of the horse till it went over. Then they went back to facing north."

b: ^"Jory. The Watch. Well, the rest of the Watch. The Captain's the Watch; I'm the running about."
^"On my rounds. The Captain says a round's a round even when nothing's round the corner. Especially then."

s0: ^"The Captain paid me this week. Out of his own purse. Don't tell him I told you. He writes it down anyway."
s1: ^"If you're going down, go down with friends. That's not the Captain talking. That's me."
s2: ^"I've never seen a bright-eyed one. I'd like to keep it that way."

b: ^"Nell Tolley. The Crossed Keys. A bed's cheap. The stairs up to it are what you pay for."
^"Water's for the guests. The well's for everyone, and everyone's at it at dawn."

s0: ^"Rest's five coppers a level. Don't ask what a level is. It's what the ledger says."
s1: ^"You look like the stairs will be a trial. They'll still cost you."
s2: ^"Maudry pours, I put people to bed. Between us, Thornwick gets by."

nell_topics: ^Three sergeants, and they never heard us.
^You walk very quietly for an innkeeper.
nell_trial_offer: ^Nell looks at your rogue for a long moment, the way she looks at a guest she suspects will leave by the window.
^"I kept an inn before this. And before that, something else. Never mind what."
^"There's sergeants in Wickham Keep who think they're hard to get behind. Put three of them down, and I'll teach your rogue what I used to do on stairs."

c-0: ^"Don't tell Maudry. She'll want to charge for it."
c-1: ^"Suit yourself. The stairs'll still creak for you."

nell_trial_active: ^"Three Redhand sergeants in the Keep. They shout. People who shout never listen for anyone behind them."
nell_trial_turnin: ^Nell takes your rogue up the Crossed Keys' stairs and back down again, twice, and the stairs don't make a sound either time.
^"Weight on the edge, not the middle. Breathe out when they breathe in. And when they turn round, be somewhere else. There. That's worth more than the room."

b: ^"Hedda. Eggs, if you want them. I know the weather, too, but I don't sell that."
^"Fog off the fields this morning. It'll burn off by noon, same as yesterday. Eggs?"
^"Wind's turning. Rain tomorrow, or not. I'm right more often than Lord Pellam."

s0: ^"The hens stopped laying the week the barrows opened. They've started again. Hens don't hold grudges."
s1: ^"Folk say the dead walk in step. So do the geese. Nobody writes to Greyholt about the geese."
s2: ^"Two for a copper, and I'll not tell anyone you bought eggs before going to fight the dead."

hedda_topics: ^It listened. Six waves in the chapel.
^Does the weather really listen to you?
hedda_trial_offer: ^"It does. Not always. Nobody listens always."
^Hedda looks at your mage the way she looks at the sky before she says whether it'll rain.
^"You've the hands for it. Go and stand in the Sunken Chapel, where it's damp and cold and full of things that don't like either. Six waves. See if the cold comes when you call it."

c-0: ^"Wrap up. I'm not joking. That's half of it."
c-1: ^"No hurry. Weather's patient. It's the only thing that is."

hedda_trial_active: ^"The Sunken Chapel. Six waves. When it's coldest, don't fight it. Ask it."
hedda_trial_turnin: ^Hedda holds out her hand, palm down, over the eggs, and for a moment there's frost on the shells.
^"There. That's all it is. A hard frost, early, and you decide where it lands. Don't tell anyone I can do that. They'll want it for the milk."
